A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 36-page MoDeGPT paper, including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original MoDeGPT experiments measuring perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, compression costs, throughput, and ablation outcomes.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same original experimental results, including compression evaluations, runtime measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the reconstruction objective, global sparsity allocation, grouped-query adaptation in Appendix B.1, and refined allocation in Appendix B.11 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same dataset and task coverage, including WikiText-2, Alpaca, PTB, and the downstream task suite described in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding comparisons, including SliceGPT, ShortGPT, SLEB, and LLM Surgeon, plus the feature-mimic, SVD, and semi-structured methods in Tables 17–19.

E3.justification: Calibration sampling, compression rates, model configurations, evaluation metrics, throughput settings, and recovery fine-tuning protocols are unchanged throughout Section 4 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: Both retain the same module and sparsity ablations, fine-tuning and combination studies, high-compression tests, generation examples, and calibration sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical throughout the main paper and appendices; there are no changes to run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports the same WikiText-2 perplexities of 7.51 and 6.10 for 30% compressed LLaMA-2 7B and 13B, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–4, Propositions 1–3, Appendix A proofs, and additional allocation equations in Appendix B.11 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about modular decomposition, theoretical guarantees, compression effectiveness, computational savings, and inference throughput.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are identical, including Appendix C's limitations concerning task bias and overfitting the reconstruction objective.

D1.justification: Implementation details, numerical precision, hyperparameters, hardware, timing information, and access information are unchanged. Appendix B.2 and the PDFs' external-link target match.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning statements, citations, and the reference list are identical; no cited works or relationships to prior research change.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes, from v4 dated 1 March 2025 to v5 dated 2 May 2025. The paper's wording, headings, and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–36 render pixel-identically; the only first-page visual difference is the stamp text.

improvement.justification: The later PDF updates only the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
